posts.full_text:
a 9B model that matches Qwen3.8-27B on AutomationBench (36.67)

SenseNova Loop 9B does it with one trick: it runs its own layers twice

it stores 32 layers and runs 56
~9B weights, ~14.6B worth of compute

what stood out to me:
> the loop. layers 4-27 run twice on the same weights
> the routing. two streams trade info through learned paths (mHC)
> the attention. three linear layers, then one full, on repeat

GAIA goes from 37.86 to 69.90 between the Preview and this release

the memory part is what I like most:
4-bit weights, 256K context, ~15 GiB of GPU memory
a 4-bit KV cache brings that down to ~12 GiB
text and images in, Apache 2.0

the quantized builds are ready to run:
> official AWQ 4-bit: 4.9 GB of weights, works with vLLM and SGLang
> GGUF: Q4_K_M is 5.82 GB, Q8_0 is 9.8 GB
> Ollama runs the GGUF in one line

my take: a loop is a cheap way to buy depth
same weights, more compute
their tests peak around 3-4 loops

I want to see where that ceiling sits on real agent work
that's my next test

posts.full_text:
Fable 5.2 just rebuilt 6 years of my life on one map. from a folder on my MacBook i didn't know existed. 41,862 texts, every location in them, every photo with GPS.

not screenshots. the actual messages. names, numbers, timestamps. photos people sent me. voice notes. my bank's login codes.

they were just sitting in an old iPhone backup. nothing in Messages on the Mac. a folder i had never opened.

opened Claude Code, picked Fable 5.2 and told it to find anything on my laptop that came from my phone. it went straight to ~/Library/Application Support/MobileSync/Backup. 6 backups. one file with a 40-character name. Fable matched it to sms.db. no password on any of it.

then i asked it to show me what's inside. 4 minutes later every location someone sent me and every photo with GPS was pinned on one map by date.

started scrolling. then i saw the newest backup was from this morning. the phone was charging on my desk while i read it.

your iPhone is encrypted. but when you back it up to a Mac, "encrypt local backup" is a box you have to tick yourself. mine was never ticked. any app i ever gave full disk access could read all of it.

ticked the box, set a password, deleted the 5 old backups. but how many apps already read that folder, i don't know.

if you want to check yours, plug your iPhone into your Mac, open Finder, click your phone and look at "encrypt local backup". if it's empty, ask Claude to look in the MobileSync folder. path above is where mine were.

the full Fable 5.2 course is in the article below ↓

4. set ONE alert to "any alert function call" and drop in your webhook URL

5. start the webhook receiver from the repo and open a free tunnel

6. every packet drops into packets/latest.json the second the candle closes

7. launch Claude Code with Fable 5.2 and feed it agent/AGENT_PROMPT.md as the prompt

8. pull the signal: you get back the call, confidence, entry, stop, targets, sizing, and the exact reason it could fail

9. one alert per chart. stack BTC, ETH and SOL and have it rank every setup

FREE and open source.

The MCP drives Blender and furnishes every empty flat on the books from the listing photos alone.

The interior is generated to match the real room, down to the window light and the floor it already has.

> MEASURE - room size read from the empty photo
> LIGHT - lamps matched to the sun in each shot
> STYLE - furniture picked for who the flat will sell to
> SWAP - three looks per room from the same photo
> LABEL - every image marked as virtually staged

Physical staging means a van, two movers and rented furniture sitting in a flat for weeks.

Empty listings sell slower online, so agencies keep paying for staging that eats their margin.

With the MCP every listing goes live furnished the same day the keys come in.

Buyers still see the real walls and windows, and only the furniture is new.

Across a few hundred listings a year that is where the $340,000 stopped going.

Before and after shots from every listing are lined up in the article below.

Stop writing better prompts

SpaceX engineer Lauren Tan doesn’t, and her Grok Bots run on their own

Here’s how she hands a real job to a bot, using client bookings as the example:

1. Don’t say "handle my bookings"

> Say "done means it’s in the system and the client got a confirmation:

2. Don’t write a 2-page prompt

> Turn on voice, talk through how you do it, and let the bot repeat it back

3. Don’t hope it guesses your rules

> Give it real cases: double bookings, wrong times, missing info

4. Don’t read complaints and shrug

> Log every step and let the bot find where the time actually went

5. Don’t keep 5 tools disconnected

> Use one ticket ID across them, so the bot can connect the dots

6. Don’t run it by hand forever

> Once it works, put it on a Routine: on an event or on a schedule
